# bicountbrms

Custom [brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/) families for Bayesian
modelling of **pairs of counts** that are positively correlated.
Applications include counts recorded by two sources that measure the
same quantity, such as two observers, two instruments, or two reporting
channels.

The pair (y_1, y_2) is modelled by **trivariate reduction**, with
Poisson components in
[`bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
(Holgate 1964; Karlis and Ntzoufras 2003) or negative-binomial
components in
[`binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
(Kirkpatrick and Neale 2016; Kirkpatrick 2022). Each count is the sum of
a latent count recorded by both sources, which induces the correlation,
and a latent count recorded by that source alone.

The native parameters of the model are the rates and (for negative
binomial) dispersions of the three latent components. The model can also
be fitted using alternative [congruence–bias
coordinates](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/reparameterisation.html),
each of which directly represents a quantity of interest when comparing
two sources: the midpoint of the two expected counts, the congruence
between the two sources, the source bias, and (for negative binomial)
the overdispersion of each component.
[`bf_mfd()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bf_mfd.md)
writes the brms formula in these coordinates, so priors and predictors
act directly on the quantities of interest, and `summary(fit)` reports
the posterior of each coordinate. The native parameterisation can be
fitted with an ordinary brms formula, in which a predictor can instead
act on a single latent component; see *Models with predictors* in
[Getting
started](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/bicountbrms.html).

The `_partialobs()` constructors fit the model when one source has
missing values, and the fitted model can impute the missing counts of
that source conditional on the recorded counts from the other source.

## The core functions

|  | both counts recorded | source 1 has missing values |
|----|----|----|
| **equidispersed** (Poisson latent counts) | [`bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md) | [`bipois_partialobs()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois_partialobs.md) |
| **overdispersed** (negative-binomial latent counts) | [`binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md) | [`binegbin_partialobs()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin_partialobs.md) |

Each row of the table is one family. The two constructors of a family
share the likelihood and the post-processing methods, and the
`_partialobs()` constructor also takes the observation indicator
`y1_obs`.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("anhsmith/bicountbrms")
```

Stan and a C++ toolchain are required. On Windows, install
[Rtools45](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools45/rtools.html).
Either `rstan` or `cmdstanr` works as the `brms` backend.

## Minimal fits

The models below are written in the [congruence–bias
coordinates](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/reparameterisation.html)
with
[`bf_mfd()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bf_mfd.md),
which takes one formula for each coordinate (`logM`, `logitf`, `delta`,
`kappas`, `kappaxone`, and `kappaxtwo`; see [Getting
started](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/bicountbrms.html)
for their definitions). y_2 is passed to the family as supplementary
integer data through `vint()`, and the Stan function for the family
through the `stanvars` argument. Both are required. brms gives every
coordinate a flat, improper prior unless one is set, and [Getting
started](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/bicountbrms.html)
gives a prior for each coordinate.

### Paired designs

``` r

library(brms)
library(bicountbrms)

fit <- brm(
  bf_mfd(
    y1 | vint(y2),
    logM      ~ 1,
    logitf    ~ 1,
    delta     ~ 1,
    kappas    ~ 1,
    kappaxone ~ 1,
    kappaxtwo ~ 1
  ),
  family   = binegbin(),
  stanvars = binegbin_stanvars(),
  data     = dat,
  prior    = priors  # one prior for each coordinate; see Getting started
)
```

### Partially paired designs

Where source 1 has missing values, the data need an observation
indicator `y1_obs`, `1` where y_1 was recorded and `0` where it was not.
**`y1` must not be `NA`**, because brms drops any row with a missing
response with only a warning. On an unpaired row, the likelihood term
does not depend on `y1`, so `y1` can be any integer. We suggest `-1`,
because it cannot be confused with a recorded count:

``` r

dat$y1_obs <- as.integer(!is.na(dat$y1))
dat$y1[is.na(dat$y1)] <- -1L
```

The indicator is passed as the second argument of `vint()`, and the
family and its stanvars are the `_partialobs` constructors:

``` r

fit_po <- brm(
  bf_mfd(
    y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs),
    logM      ~ 1,
    logitf    ~ 1,
    delta     ~ 1,
    kappas    ~ 1,
    kappaxone ~ 1,
    kappaxtwo ~ 1
  ),
  family   = binegbin_partialobs(),
  stanvars = binegbin_partialobs_stanvars(),
  data     = dat,
  prior    = priors
)
```

To impute y_1 on the rows where it was not recorded, use
[`posterior_predict_y1_given_y2()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/posterior_predict_y1_given_y2.md);
see [Prediction and
imputation](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/prediction.html).

## Documentation

- [Getting
  started](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/bicountbrms.html)
  describes one
  [`binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  analysis from start to finish: simulating data from known parameters,
  fitting the model in the congruence–bias parameterisation, checking
  recovery of the generating values, predicting both counts, and
  comparing the fit with a Poisson model.
- [Partially paired
  designs](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/partially-paired-designs.html)
  fits a model in the congruence–bias parameterisation to simulated data
  in which source 1 has missing values, and compares the imputed values
  of y_1, given y_2 and marginal, with values withheld from the model.
- [Prediction and
  imputation](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/prediction.html)
  describes the prediction functions and the imputation of y_1 on
  unpaired rows.
- [The congruence–bias
  parameterisation](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/reparameterisation.html)
  has an interactive widget that simulates pairs of counts from one
  model and shows the congruence–bias and native parameterisations side
  by side, and gives the equations that convert between the coordinates
  and the native parameters.
- The
  [changelog](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/news/index.html)
  records what each release changed.

A companion package,
[`skellambrms`](https://github.com/anhsmith/skellambrms), supplies
Skellam, discrete Laplace, and discrete normal families that model d =
y_1 - y_2 directly, with optional truncation via
[`resp_trunc()`](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/reference/addition-terms.html).

## References

*Biometrika* **51**(1–2), 241–245. <https://doi.org/10.2307/2334210>

Karlis, D. and Ntzoufras, I. (2003). Analysis of sports data by using
bivariate Poisson models. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society:
Series D (The Statistician)* **52**(3), 381–393.
<https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9884.00366>

Kirkpatrick, R. M. (2022). *RMKdiscrete: Sundry discrete probability
distributions*. R package version 0.2.
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=RMKdiscrete>

Kirkpatrick, R. M. and Neale, M. C. (2016). Applying multivariate
discrete distributions to genetically informative count data. *Behavior
Genetics* **46**(2), 252–268.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/s10519-015-9757-z>

# Package index

## Families for paired counts

Constructors for the bipois and binegbin families, which model a pair of
counts by trivariate reduction with Poisson or negative-binomial
components. Each family has a second constructor for partially paired
designs, listed below, and the two constructors of a family share a
likelihood and the post-processing methods.

- [`bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
  [`bipois_stanvars()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
  [`log_lik_bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
  [`posterior_predict_bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
  [`posterior_epred_bipois()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois.md)
  : Joint bivariate-Poisson custom family for brms
- [`binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  [`binegbin_stanvars()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  [`log_lik_binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  [`posterior_predict_binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  [`posterior_epred_binegbin()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin.md)
  : Joint bivariate custom family with negative-binomial components for
  brms

## Partially paired designs

Constructors for partially paired designs, in which source 1 has missing
values. On an unpaired row, the likelihood term is the marginal
probability of y2, so the row informs the shared component and the
exclusive component of source 2.

- [`bipois_partialobs()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois_partialobs.md)
  [`bipois_partialobs_stanvars()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bipois_partialobs.md)
  : Joint bivariate-Poisson family for partially observed pairs
- [`binegbin_partialobs()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin_partialobs.md)
  [`binegbin_partialobs_stanvars()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/binegbin_partialobs.md)
  : Joint bivariate family with negative-binomial components for
  partially observed pairs

## Prediction and imputation

Draws and expectations of both counts together, and of y1 given the
recorded y2. The functions conditional on y2 impute y1 on the unpaired
rows of a fit from bipois_partialobs() or binegbin_partialobs().

- [`posterior_predict_y1_and_y2()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/posterior_predict_y1_and_y2.md)
  [`posterior_epred_y1_and_y2()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/posterior_predict_y1_and_y2.md)
  : Draws and expectations of both counts from the joint model
- [`posterior_predict_y1_given_y2()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/posterior_predict_y1_given_y2.md)
  [`posterior_epred_y1_given_y2()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/posterior_predict_y1_given_y2.md)
  : Draws and expectations of y1 given y2

## Congruence–bias coordinates

Conversion between the native parameters and the congruence–bias
coordinates (the midpoint of the two expected counts, the congruence,
and the source bias), and the brms formula for a model in the
coordinates.

- [`mfd_to_dpars()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/mfd_to_dpars.md)
  : Convert from the congruence–bias parameterisation to native
  parameters
- [`dpars_to_mfd()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/dpars_to_mfd.md)
  : Convert from native parameters to the congruence–bias
  parameterisation
- [`bf_mfd()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/bf_mfd.md)
  : Build a brms formula in the congruence–bias parameterisation

## Simulation

Random generation of paired counts from the generating model of the
bipois and binegbin families, with the shared and source-exclusive
components of each pair.

- [`rbicount()`](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/reference/rbicount.md)
  : Random generation of paired counts

# Articles

### Using the families

- [Getting started with
  bicountbrms](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/bicountbrms.md):

- [The congruence–bias
  parameterisation](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/reparameterisation.md):

  The congruence–bias coordinates, an interactive widget showing one
  model in the congruence–bias and native parameterisations, and the map
  between the coordinates and the native parameters.

- [Partially paired
  designs](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/partially-paired-designs.md):

  Fitting a partially paired design in the congruence–bias
  parameterisation, and imputing the counts that the partially observed
  source did not record.

- [Prediction and
  imputation](https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/articles/prediction.md):
